nordamerika.explanation: "Nordamerika" means "North America", the big area with Canada, the USA and Mexico. It is built from nord (north) and Amerika (America).

sentence.da: Hun bor i **Nordamerika**, i Canada.
sentence.en: She lives in North America, in Canada.

norden.explanation: "Norden" means "the Nordic countries": Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland, often with Greenland, the Faroe Islands and Åland. It is written with an uppercase N.

sentence.da: Mange rejser mellem landene i **Norden** uden pas.
sentence.en: Many people travel between the countries of the Nordic region without a passport.

nordisk.explanation: "Nordisk" means "Nordic", for Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland together and what they share: "nordisk mad" (Nordic food).

sentence.da: Danmark og Sverige har en **nordisk** velfærdsmodel.
sentence.en: Denmark and Sweden have a Nordic welfare model.

nordlig.explanation: "Nordlig" means "northern", the north part of a place: "Skagen ligger i det nordlige Danmark" (Skagen is in northern Denmark). For wind it also means "from the north".

sentence.da: Vinden er **nordlig**, og det er koldt.
sentence.en: The wind is from the north, and it is cold.

nordlys.explanation: "Et nordlys" means "northern lights", the green and sometimes red or purple glow seen in the sky far in the north. You mostly see it in places such as Norway, Iceland and Greenland. It is built from nord (north) and et lys (a light).

sentence.da: Vi så **nordlys** over fjorden i Norge.
sentence.en: We saw northern lights over the fjord in Norway.

nordpå.explanation: "Nordpå" means "northward", toward the north: "Vi kører nordpå" (We drive north). To name where a place is located, use "i nord" (in the north): "Skoven ligger i nord" (The forest lies in the north).

sentence.da: Fuglene flyver **nordpå** om foråret.
sentence.en: The birds fly north in the spring.

nordsøen.explanation: "Nordsøen" means "the North Sea", the sea along the west coast of Jylland (Jutland).

sentence.da: **Nordsøen** ligger vest for Danmark.
sentence.en: The North Sea lies west of Denmark.

norge.explanation: "Norge" means "Norway". The language is "norsk" (Norwegian), a different word from the country name.

sentence.da: Min ven kommer fra **Norge** og taler norsk.
sentence.en: My friend comes from Norway and speaks Norwegian.

normal.explanation: "Normal" means "normal", what is usual and as expected: "Det er helt normalt" (That is completely normal). It is spelled the same as in English.

sentence.da: En **normal** kropstemperatur er 37 grader.
sentence.en: A normal body temperature is 37 degrees.

norsk.explanation: "Norsk" means "Norwegian", both for things from Norway and for the language. Danish writes it with a lowercase letter: "Jeg taler norsk" (I speak Norwegian).

sentence.da: I Oslo taler man **norsk**.
sentence.en: In Oslo people speak Norwegian.

nougat.explanation: "Nougat" means "nougat", a soft, sweet brown filling often found inside chocolate.

sentence.da: Man laver **nougat** af nødder og sukker.
sentence.en: You make nougat from nuts and sugar.

november.explanation: "November" means "November" and is spelled the same as in English. Danish writes month names with a lowercase letter, even in the middle of a sentence: "i november" (in November).

sentence.da: Det er mørkt og gråt i **november**.
sentence.en: It is dark and gray in November.

nu.explanation: "Nu" means "now". Danes also drop "nu" into a sentence to soften it, with no idea of time: "Det er nu ikke så svært" (It is not that hard, really).

sentence.da: Jeg skal gå **nu**.
sentence.en: I have to go now.

nu skal du høre.explanation: "Nu skal du høre" means "now listen", literally "now you will hear". People say it to get attention just before telling a story or news.

forms.da: Nu skal du høre, hvad jeg har at sige.
forms.en: Now listen to what I have to say.

sentence.da: Vent, **nu skal du høre**, jeg har en god nyhed.
sentence.en: Wait, now listen, I have good news.

nudler.explanation: "Nudler" means "noodles", long thin strips of dough, boiled and eaten with sauce or vegetables.

sentence.da: Jeg koger **nudler** i vand.
sentence.en: I boil noodles in water.

nul.explanation: "Nul" means "zero". In sports scores it is "nil": "Vi vinder to–nul" (We win two–nil).

sentence.da: Vandet bliver til is ved **nul** grader.
sentence.en: Water turns to ice at zero degrees.

nutid.explanation: "En nutid" means "a present tense", the verb form for what is happening now: "jeg løber" (I run) is in the present tense.

sentence.da: Sætningen Jeg spiser et æble står i **nutid**.
sentence.en: The sentence I eat an apple is in the present tense.

nutiden.explanation: "Nutiden" means "the present", the time we live in now. Use it when you talk about modern life, as in "nutidens unge" (the young people of today).

sentence.da: Vi lærer om fortiden, men vi lever i **nutiden**.
sentence.en: We learn about the past, but we live in the present.

nutildags.explanation: "Nutildags" means "nowadays", used to compare now with earlier times: "Nutildags har alle en telefon" (Nowadays everyone has a phone). It is also written as three words, "nu til dags" (literally, "now to day"), with the same meaning.

sentence.da: Før skrev vi breve, men **nutildags** skriver vi beskeder.
sentence.en: Before, we wrote letters, but nowadays we write messages.

nuttet.explanation: "Nuttet" means "cute" and is used for small things that make you smile, such as babies, puppies and kittens.

sentence.da: Din lille hund er så **nuttet**.
sentence.en: Your little dog is so cute.

nuvel.explanation: "Nuvel" means "very well" or "well now". You say it to accept something and move on: "Nuvel, så gør vi det" (Very well, we will do it that way). It sounds a bit old-fashioned.

sentence.da: **Nuvel**, så er det aftalt, og vi mødes klokken ni.
sentence.en: Very well, then it is agreed, and we meet at nine.

nuværende.explanation: "Nuværende" means "current" or "present", for what applies at this moment, not earlier or later. It goes before the word it describes: "den nuværende regering" (the current government).

sentence.da: Min **nuværende** chef er sød, men min tidligere var streng.
sentence.en: My current boss is nice, but my former one was strict.

ny.explanation: "Ny" means "new", for something just made, just bought or not used before. It is also part of "nytår" (new year), as in "godt nytår" (happy new year).

sentence.da: Jeg har købt en **ny** telefon.
sentence.en: I have bought a new phone.

nyheder.explanation: "Nyheder" means "news". Danish treats it as plural: "Nyhederne er dårlige" (The news is bad; literally, "the news are bad").

sentence.da: Jeg læser **nyheder** i avisen hver morgen.
sentence.en: I read the news in the newspaper every morning.

nylig.explanation: "Nylig" means "recently" and is built from ny (new). You almost always say "for nylig" (recently), with "for" (for) in front: "Jeg mødte hende for nylig" (I met her recently).

sentence.da: Jeg mødte hende for **nylig** i byen.
sentence.en: I met her recently in town.

nysgerrig.explanation: "Nysgerrig" means "curious" and describes someone who wants to know things: "Han er nysgerrig efter at lære mere" (He is curious to learn more). It can also mean nosy: "Vær ikke så nysgerrig!" (Don't be so nosy!)

sentence.da: Min søn er **nysgerrig** og stiller mange spørgsmål.
sentence.en: My son is curious and asks many questions.

nysgerrighed.explanation: "En nysgerrighed" means "curiosity", the wish to find out or know more. It comes from "nysgerrig" (curious) with "-hed" on the end, like "-ness" in English. The same ending turns "fri" (free) into "en frihed" (a freedom).

sentence.da: Børn stiller mange spørgsmål af **nysgerrighed**.
sentence.en: Children ask many questions out of curiosity.

nytte.explanation: "En nytte" means "use" or "benefit", the good you get out of something. Danes also say "gøre nytte" (to be of use) for a thing or person that helps: "Paraplyen gjorde nytte" (The umbrella was useful).

sentence.da: Jeg har stor **nytte** af min nye ordbog.
sentence.en: I get great use out of my new dictionary.

nyttig.explanation: "Nyttig" means "useful": "Det er et nyttigt tip" (That is a useful tip).

sentence.da: Paraplyen er **nyttig**, når det regner.
sentence.en: The umbrella is useful when it rains.

nytårsaften.explanation: "Nytårsaften" means "New Year's Eve", the evening of 31 December. It is made from nytår (new year) and aften (evening).

sentence.da: På **nytårsaften** siger vi "godt nytår" ved midnat.
sentence.en: On New Year's Eve we say "happy new year" at midnight.

nå.explanation: "Nå" means "oh" or "well". You say it when you understand something or are a little surprised: "Nå, det vidste jeg ikke!" (Oh, I did not know that!)

sentence.da: **Nå**, nu forstår jeg det!
sentence.en: Oh, now I understand!

nå ja.explanation: "Nå ja" means "oh right" and shows you just remembered or understood something. It often comes with the small word "jo" (as you know): "Nå ja, det er jo tirsdag i dag" (Oh right, it's Tuesday today, you know).

forms.da: Nå ja, nu husker jeg det.

sentence.da: **Nå ja**, jeg skal jo hente børnene.
sentence.en: Oh right, I have to pick up the kids.

nå men.explanation: "Nå men" means "well then" and you say it to move a conversation on or to wrap it up: "Nå men, så går vi i gang" (Well then, let's get started).

forms.da: Nå men, lad os komme i gang.

forms.en: Well then, I have to move on.

sentence.da: **Nå men**, nu må jeg hellere gå.
sentence.en: Well then, I had better go now.

nåde.explanation: "En nåde" means "mercy" or "grace": kindness shown to someone who could have been punished.

sentence.da: Fangen bad dommeren om **nåde**, men fik ingen.
sentence.en: The prisoner asked the judge for mercy, but got none.

når.explanation: "Når" means "when" or "whenever" for things that happen again and again or have not happened yet: "Når det regner, bliver jeg hjemme" (When it rains, I stay home). For one time in the past, use "da" (when): "Da jeg kom hjem, var det mørkt" (When I came home, it was dark). To ask a question, use "hvornår" (when): "Hvornår kommer du?" (When are you coming?).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer, **når** jeg kommer hjem.
sentence.en: I will call when I get home.

når som helst.explanation: "Når som helst" means "anytime", or "whenever". It can also mean "at any moment", for something that might happen without warning: "Det kan regne når som helst" (It can rain at any moment).

forms.da: Jeg har tid når som helst.

sentence.da: Du kan ringe til mig **når som helst**.
sentence.en: You can call me anytime.

næppe.explanation: "Næppe" means "hardly" or "barely", for something very unlikely: "Han kommer næppe" (He is unlikely to come). A tiny chance is left, unlike "aldrig" (never).

forms.en: She is unlikely to come today

sentence.da: Vi får **næppe** sne, fordi det er for varmt.
sentence.en: We are unlikely to get snow because it is too warm.

nær.explanation: "Nær" means "close" or "near". Use it for people you are close to: "en nær ven" (a close friend). For places, "tæt på" (close to) is more common: "tæt på stationen" (close to the station).

sentence.da: Han er en **nær** ven af mig.
sentence.en: He is a close friend of mine.

nærig.explanation: "Nærig" means "stingy", not wanting to spend or give away money even when it would be fair. It is a negative word about a person, unlike "sparsommelig" (thrifty), which is a good quality.

sentence.da: Han er **nærig** og giver aldrig drikkepenge.
sentence.en: He is stingy and never gives tips.

næringsrig.explanation: "Næringsrig" means "nutritious", full of vitamins, protein and other things the body needs. It is built from en næring (nourishment) and rig (rich).

sentence.da: Grønkål er **næringsrig**, fordi den indeholder meget jern.
sentence.en: Kale is nutritious because it contains a lot of iron.

nærmest.explanation: "Nærmest" means "almost". For a place it means "nearest": "den nærmeste station" (the nearest station).

sentence.da: Opgaven var **nærmest** umulig at løse på en dag.
sentence.en: The task was almost impossible to solve in one day.

nærværende.explanation: "Nærværende" means "present" in the sense of really being there with your full attention, not just in the room. In formal papers, "nærværende kontrakt" means "this contract".

sentence.da: Min læge er **nærværende** og lytter, når jeg taler.
sentence.en: My doctor is attentive and listens when I speak.

næseblod.explanation: "Næseblod" means "a nosebleed", blood running from the nose. Danes say it without "et": "Jeg har næseblod" (I have a nosebleed).

sentence.da: Når man får **næseblod**, skal man læne sig frem.
sentence.en: When you get a nosebleed, you should lean forward.

næsten.explanation: "Næsten" means "almost": "Jeg er næsten færdig" (I am almost done). Do not mix it up with "næste" (next): "næste uge" (next week).

sentence.da: Jeg er **næsten** færdig med arbejdet.
sentence.en: I am almost done with the work.

næsten aldrig.explanation: "Næsten aldrig" means "almost never". It is built from næsten (almost) and aldrig (never). "Aldrig" already makes it a no, so do not add "ikke" (not): "Hun spiser næsten aldrig kød" (She almost never eats meat).

sentence.da: Han kommer **næsten aldrig** for sent.
sentence.en: He almost never comes late.

nødder.explanation: "Nødder" means "nuts" of all kinds, like hazelnuts and walnuts.

sentence.da: Egern elsker at spise **nødder**.
sentence.en: Squirrels love to eat nuts.

nødhjælp.explanation: "Nødhjælp" means "emergency aid", quick help sent to people after an earthquake, a war or a famine, such as food, water and medicine. It is meant for many people at once, not for one hurt person.

sentence.da: Efter jordskælvet sendte landene **nødhjælp** til området.
sentence.en: After the earthquake the countries sent emergency aid to the area.

nødig.explanation: "Nødig" means "reluctantly" and almost always comes after "vil" or "ville" (want, would). Use it to say you would rather not, as a soft no: "Jeg vil nødig tage afsted" (I would rather not leave).

forms.en: I would rather not go alone.
She would rather not say it.

forms.da: Vi vil nødig komme for sent.
forms.en: We would rather not be late.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **nødig** forstyrre dig, når du arbejder.
sentence.en: I would rather not disturb you when you are working.

nødt til.explanation: "Nødt til" means "have to" when you have no choice. To name what you must do, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg er nødt til at gå" (I have to go). If you choose to go, say "Jeg vil gå" (I want to go) instead.

forms.da: jeg er nødt til at gå
du er nødt til at vente
vi er nødt til at tale

sentence.da: Jeg er **nødt til** at gå nu.
sentence.en: I have to go now.

nødvendig.explanation: "Nødvendig" means "necessary", stronger than "vigtig" (important), because you cannot do without it: "Et pas er nødvendigt" (A passport is necessary).

sentence.da: Vand er **nødvendig**, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: Water is necessary when it is hot.

nødvendigvis.explanation: "Nødvendigvis" means "necessarily" and is nearly always used with "ikke" (not): "Han er ikke nødvendigvis rig" (He is not necessarily rich) means he may be rich or he may not be. Use it to avoid claiming something is true every time.

sentence.da: Den dyreste bil er ikke **nødvendigvis** den bedste.
sentence.en: The most expensive car is not necessarily the best.

nøgen.explanation: "Nøgen" means "naked", with no clothes on. It can also describe trees with no leaves: "nøgne træer" (trees with no leaves).

sentence.da: Han sprang **nøgen** i havet.
sentence.en: He jumped naked into the sea.

nøgtern.explanation: "Nøgtern" means "matter-of-fact" or "sober": calm and plain, without drama or strong feelings: "en nøgtern beskrivelse" (a matter-of-fact description). For "not drunk", say "ædru" (sober).

sentence.da: Han gav en **nøgtern** beskrivelse af ulykken og overdrev ikke.
sentence.en: He gave a matter-of-fact description of the accident and did not exaggerate.

nøjagtig.explanation: "Nøjagtig" means "exact" or "accurate", with no mistakes: "Klokken er nøjagtigt tolv" (It is exactly twelve o'clock). "Nøjagtigt!" (Exactly!) is also used as a one-word reply.

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en **nøjagtig** måling.
sentence.en: We need an exact measurement.

nøjagtigt.explanation: "Nøjagtigt" means "exactly", with no difference at all in time, size or amount: "nøjagtigt tre" (exactly three). Use "omtrent" (about) when it is not exact: "omtrent tre" (about three).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge **nøjagtigt** to hundrede gram mel.
sentence.en: You must use exactly two hundred grams of flour.

nøje.explanation: "Nøje" means "closely" or "carefully": with exact attention to every detail. It usually comes at the end: "Læs den nøje" (Read it closely).

forms.en: It does not matter that much

sentence.da: Man skal studere planen **nøje**, før man skriver under.
sentence.en: You must study the plan closely before you sign.

at observere.explanation: "At observere" means "to observe", to watch something closely in order to learn from it: "at observere fuglene" (to observe the birds).

sentence.da: Lægen vil **observere** patienten natten over.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to observe the patient overnight.

at offentliggøre.explanation: "At offentliggøre" means "to publish / make public", to let everyone know something that was private. You use it when a result or a decision is announced: "Regeringen offentliggør planen" (The government makes the plan public).

sentence.da: Avisen vil **offentliggøre** resultaterne på mandag.
sentence.en: The newspaper will publish the results on Monday.

at ofre.explanation: "At ofre" means "to sacrifice", to give up something valuable for a person or a goal, such as time or money: "Hun ofrer sin weekend" (She gives up her weekend). It is also used for an offering to a god: "at ofre til guderne" (to make an offering to the gods).

sentence.da: Mange forældre vil **ofre** alt for deres børn.
sentence.en: Many parents will sacrifice everything for their children.

at omdanne.explanation: "At omdanne" means "to transform", to change something completely into a new form or use. You can say it about a person too: "Oplevelsen omdannede ham" (The experience transformed him).

sentence.da: De vil **omdanne** den gamle fabrik til billige lejligheder.
sentence.en: They want to turn the old factory into cheap apartments.

sentence.da: Billetten kan **omfatte** både mad og drikke.
sentence.en: The ticket can include both food and drinks.

at omformulere.explanation: "At omformulere" means "to rephrase", to say or write the same thing again in other words. You say it when something was unclear: "Kan du omformulere det?" (Can you rephrase that?)

sentence.da: Hvis folk ikke forstår dig, må du **omformulere** spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: If people do not understand you, you have to rephrase the question.

at omgive.explanation: "At omgive" means "to surround": to be on all sides of something: "En mur omgiver byen" (A wall surrounds the town). You often see it as "omgivet af" (surrounded by): "Huset er omgivet af skov" (The house is surrounded by forest).

sentence.da: Man kan **omgive** en have med en grøn hæk.
sentence.en: You can surround a garden with a green hedge.

at omgå.explanation: "At omgå" means "to bypass" or "to get around" a problem, a rule or an obstacle, often by finding a clever way past: "omgå et problem" (get around a problem). Do not mix it up with "at omgås" (to socialize), which only adds an "s".

sentence.da: Lastbilen må **omgå** byen, fordi broen er lukket.
sentence.en: The truck has to go around the town because the bridge is closed.

at omgås.explanation: "At omgås" means "to associate with" or "to socialize": to spend time with people regularly: "Jeg omgås mest folk fra arbejdet" (I mostly spend time with people from work). Do not mix it up with "at omgå" (to bypass), which has no "s".

sentence.da: Det er rart at **omgås** mennesker, som man har det godt med.
sentence.en: It is nice to socialize with people you feel good with.

at omringe.explanation: "At omringe" means "to surround", to stand on all sides of someone or something so that there is no way past. It is used for people, such as crowds and soldiers, and also for things: "En mur omringer haven" (A wall surrounds the garden).

sentence.da: Politiet vil **omringe** huset, så ingen kan flygte.
sentence.en: The police want to surround the house so nobody can flee.

at omstille sig.explanation: "At omstille sig" means "to adapt", to change how you work or live when the situation changes, for example after new rules or a new job. "Sig" means "yourself" and changes with the person: "jeg omstiller mig" (I adapt), "du omstiller dig" (you adapt), "de omstiller sig" (they adapt).

sentence.da: Firmaet må **omstille sig**, når kunderne vil købe på nettet.
sentence.en: The company has to adapt when customers want to buy online.

at omstrukturere.explanation: "At omstrukturere" means "to restructure": to arrange something in a new way, such as a company, a school or a system: "Kommunen omstrukturerer sine skoler" (The city is restructuring its schools). The "om" at the start works like "re-" in other words, such as "at omskrive" (to rewrite).

sentence.da: Firmaet er nødt til at **omstrukturere**, fordi salget falder.
sentence.en: The company has to restructure because sales are falling.

at omtale.explanation: "At omtale" means "to mention" or "to refer to", to speak of a person or thing, often in a newspaper or in public. To say how someone is described, add "som" (as): "Hun omtales som byens bedste kok" (She is referred to as the best cook in town).

sentence.da: Aviserne kan **omtale** en ny film, før den kommer i biografen.
sentence.en: The newspapers can mention a new movie before it comes to the movie theater.

at opbevare.explanation: "At opbevare" means "to store", to keep something in a place until it is needed or so that it stays safe, such as food, documents, tools or medicine.

sentence.da: Du kan **opbevare** cyklen i kælderen om vinteren.
sentence.en: You can store the bike in the basement in winter.

at opbygge.explanation: "At opbygge" means "to build up", to create something that grows slowly step by step, such as a business, muscles or trust. For a house, use "at bygge" (to build) instead.

sentence.da: Man kan ikke **opbygge** stærke muskler på én uge.
sentence.en: You cannot build up strong muscles in one week.

at opdage.explanation: "At opdage" means "to discover": to find or notice something you did not know about: "Jeg opdagede en fejl" (I noticed a mistake). It often comes as a surprise: "Hun opdagede, at tasken var væk" (She discovered that the bag was gone).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **opdage** nye steder på rejsen.
sentence.en: We would like to discover new places on the trip.

at opdatere.explanation: "At opdatere" means "to update", to make something new or current, such as a program or a list.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **opdatere** min telefon i aften.
sentence.en: I want to update my phone tonight.

at opdele.explanation: "At opdele" means "to divide", to split something into several parts or groups: "Læreren opdeler klassen i fire hold" (The teacher splits the class into four teams). "At dele" (to share) is used more for giving a part to someone else: "Jeg deler kagen med dig" (I share the cake with you).

sentence.da: Vi kan **opdele** kagen i otte lige store stykker.
sentence.en: We can divide the cake into eight equal pieces.

at opdrage.explanation: "At opdrage" means "to raise (a child)", to teach a child how to behave.

sentence.da: Forældre skal **opdrage** deres børn til at sige tak og undskyld.
sentence.en: Parents must raise their children to say thank you and sorry.

at operere.explanation: "At operere" means "to operate", on a patient: "Lægen opererer i morgen" (The doctor operates tomorrow). It is also used for a business working somewhere: "Firmaet opererer i Europa" (The company operates in Europe).

sentence.da: Lægen skal **operere** min mor i morgen.
sentence.en: The doctor is going to operate on my mother tomorrow.

at opfange.explanation: "At opfange" means "to pick up" or "to catch" something that is sent or passing by, such as a sound, a signal or a message.

sentence.da: Antennen kan **opfange** signaler fra satellitter langt væk.
sentence.en: The antenna can pick up signals from far-away satellites.

at opfatte.explanation: "At opfatte" means "to perceive" and has two uses. For how you see a person or a situation: "Hvordan opfatter du ham?" (How do you see him?). For catching words you hear: "Jeg opfattede ikke navnet" (I did not catch the name).

sentence.da: Børn kan **opfatte** mere, end de voksne tror.
sentence.en: Children can perceive more than the adults think.

at opfinde.explanation: "At opfinde" means "to invent", to make something completely new that did not exist before. It also means to make up a story: "Han opfandt en undskyldning" (He made up an excuse).

sentence.da: Hun vil **opfinde** en maskine, som kan rydde op.
sentence.en: She wants to invent a machine that can tidy up.

at opfordre.explanation: "At opfordre" means "to urge" or "to encourage", to ask someone strongly to do something, often in public: "Politiet opfordrer folk til at blive hjemme" (The police urge people to stay at home). To lift someone's mood, use "at opmuntre" (to cheer up): "Hun opmuntrede mig" (She cheered me up).

sentence.da: Vi vil **opfordre** alle til at stemme ved valget.
sentence.en: We want to urge everyone to vote in the election.

at opfylde.explanation: "At opfylde" means "to fulfill", to do what a promise, a hope or a rule asks for.

sentence.da: Du skal **opfylde** alle kravene, før du kan søge.
sentence.en: You must fulfill all the requirements before you can apply.

at opføre.explanation: "At opføre" means "to build" or "to perform". For building, "at opføre" is used for larger buildings: "Kommunen opfører en ny skole" (The council is building a new school). For performing, it means to put on a play or a show: "Teatret opfører et stykke" (The theater is putting on a play). You can tell which meaning is intended from the context of the sentence. With "sig" (oneself), "at opføre" means "to behave": "at opføre sig pænt" (to behave nicely).

sentence.da: Teatret vil **opføre** et stykke af Holberg i efteråret.
sentence.en: The theater will stage a play by Holberg in the fall.

at opføre sig.explanation: "At opføre sig" means "to behave", and it needs a word like "pænt" (nicely) or "dårligt" (badly): "Han opfører sig dårligt" (He behaves badly). Without "sig" (oneself), "at opføre" means "to build": "De opfører et hus" (They are building a house).

sentence.da: Børn skal **opføre sig** pænt i skolen.
sentence.en: Children must behave nicely at school.

at opgive.explanation: "At opgive" means "to give up", to quit trying because it seems impossible or not worth it: "Hun opgav at finde nøglen" (She gave up looking for the key). It also means to give information: "at opgive et navn" (to give a name).

sentence.da: Vi vil aldrig **opgive**, selv når det bliver svært.
sentence.en: We will never give up, even when it gets hard.

at opgradere.explanation: "At opgradere" means "to upgrade", to replace something with a newer or stronger version, such as a phone, a program or a plan: "Jeg opgraderer mit abonnement" (I upgrade my subscription). It is built like the English word, with "op" (up) in front. For making something better in any way, use "at forbedre" (to improve).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **opgradere** telefonen, før den bliver for langsom.
sentence.en: I want to upgrade the phone before it gets too slow.

at opgøre.explanation: "At opgøre" means "to calculate" or "to settle": to add everything up and find the final amount: "opgøre regnskabet" (settle the accounts), "opgøre skaden" (calculate the damage).

sentence.da: Banken kan **opgøre** gælden, så vi ved det præcise beløb.
sentence.en: The bank can calculate the debt so we know the exact amount.

at ophæve.explanation: "At ophæve" means "to repeal" or "to lift": to officially end a rule or a decision: "ophæve en lov" (repeal a law), "ophæve en regel" (lift a rule).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **ophæve** forbuddet mod at tage hunde med i parken.
sentence.en: The city will lift the ban on bringing dogs to the park.

at ophøre.explanation: "At ophøre" means "to cease", to come to an end, usually for something that has been going on: "Støjen ophører klokken ti" (The noise ceases at ten). It sounds official, such as in letters and announcements. In everyday speech people say "at holde op" (to stop): "Hold op!" (Stop it!)

sentence.da: Ordningen kan **ophøre**, hvis ingen længere bruger den.
sentence.en: The scheme can cease if nobody uses it any more.

at opklare.explanation: "At opklare" means "to solve (a case)", to find out the truth about a crime or a mystery. It can also mean to clear up a misunderstanding: "Vi må opklare, hvad der skete" (We must find out what happened). For puzzles and math problems, use "at løse" (to solve).

sentence.da: Politiet kan **opklare** sagen, hvis nogen har set noget.
sentence.en: The police can solve the case if somebody has seen something.

at oplade.explanation: "At oplade" means "to charge", to fill a battery with power: "Jeg oplader min computer" (I charge my computer). In daily speech, people often drop "op" (up) and say "at lade" (to charge): "Jeg lader min telefon" (I am charging my phone).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **oplade** min telefon i nat.
sentence.en: I have to charge my phone tonight.

at opleve.explanation: "At opleve" means "to experience", to go through something yourself.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **opleve** Italien en dag.
sentence.en: I would like to experience Italy one day.

at oplyse.explanation: "At oplyse" means "to inform" or "to light up". For "to inform", it means to give someone facts, such as news from an authority: "Politiet oplyser, at manden er fundet" (The police say the man has been found). For "to light up", it is used for places: "Månen oplyser vejen" (The moon lights up the road).

sentence.da: Kan du **oplyse**, hvornår toget kommer?
sentence.en: Can you tell me when the train comes?

at oplære.explanation: "At oplære" means "to train": to show a person how to do the practical work of a job, step by step: "Butikken oplærer ham i at bruge kassen" (The store trains him to use the register). For sports and exercise, Danes say "at træne" (to work out) instead.

sentence.da: Hun skal **oplære** den nye medarbejder i at bruge maskinen.
sentence.en: She has to train the new employee to use the machine.

at opmuntre.explanation: "At opmuntre" means "to encourage" or "to cheer up", to give someone courage or a better mood when they feel down: "Læreren opmuntrede hende til at prøve igen" (The teacher encouraged her to try again). To ask someone strongly to act, use "at opfordre" (to urge).

sentence.da: Et par rare ord kan **opmuntre** en, der er ked af det.
sentence.en: A few kind words can cheer up someone who is sad.

at opnå.explanation: "At opnå" means "to achieve", to end up with a result through effort or time: "at opnå et godt resultat" (to achieve a good result). It also works for a result you reach with other people, such as an agreement: "at opnå enighed" (to come to an agreement).

sentence.da: Hun vil **opnå** en høj karakter, fordi hun læser hver dag.
sentence.en: She wants to achieve a high grade because she studies every day.

at opprioritere.explanation: "At opprioritere" means "to prioritize higher": to make something more important than before, with more attention and funding: "opprioritere ældreplejen" (give elder care more attention). The "op" works like "up" in English.

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **opprioritere** skolerne og bruge flere penge på dem.
sentence.en: The city will give schools higher priority and spend more money on them.

at opretholde.explanation: "At opretholde" means "to maintain", to keep something going in the same state. Use it for something that would soon fail without effort: "Politiet opretholder ordenen" (The police maintain order), "Vi må opretholde kontakten" (We must keep up the contact). For cleaning and repairing a building or machine, use "at vedligeholde" (to keep in repair).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **opretholde** gode vaner uden en fast plan.
sentence.en: It is hard to keep up good habits without a fixed plan.

at oprette.explanation: "At oprette" means "to set up" or "to create", to make something official that did not exist before, such as an account, a company or a file: "Jeg opretter en konto" (I create an account). To put a thing in place, such as a shelf, use "at opsætte" (to set up): "Jeg opsætter hylden" (I put up the shelf).

sentence.da: Du skal **oprette** en bruger, før du kan logge ind.
sentence.en: You have to create a user before you can log in.

at opsige.explanation: "At opsige" means "to cancel" or "to terminate" something that runs over time, such as a job, a lease or a subscription, with notice: "Jeg har opsagt min lejlighed" (I have given notice on my apartment). For your own job, say "opsige sin stilling" (resign).

sentence.da: Du kan **opsige** abonnementet med en måneds varsel.
sentence.en: You can cancel the subscription with a month's notice.

at opstille.explanation: "At opstille" means "to set up" or "to nominate". To set up is to put things in position: "Vi opstiller teltet" (We set up the tent). In politics it means to put someone forward for election: "Partiet opstiller Lars til valget" (The party puts Lars forward for the election).

sentence.da: Vi skal **opstille** stolene i rækker, før gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: We have to set up the chairs in rows before the guests come.
